topic: Preamble and Salient Features of Indian Constitution
description: The Preamble embodies the basic philosophy, fundamental values, and objectives of the Indian Constitution. The Constitution itself is renowned for its unique features, including its comprehensive nature, quasi-federal structure, and democratic parliamentary system.

sections.title: Introduction and History of the Preamble
sections.description: The Preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and is often referred to as the key to the minds of its makers.

historical_events.significance: Introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly, laying down the philosophical foundations of the Constitution. The Preamble is based on this resolution.
Unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly, heavily influencing the eventual shaping of the Constitution.

important_facts.fact: Eminent jurist N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'.

The concept of a written Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of the USA, while its language and ideals (like Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity) were inspired by the French and Russian Revolutions, as well as the Australian Constitution.

sections.title: Key Ideals and Philosophy of the Preamble
sections.description: The Preamble outlines the nature of the Indian State and the fundamental objectives it seeks to secure for its citizens.

key_concepts.explanation: India is internally supreme and externally free. It is not a dependency or dominion of any other nation and is free to conduct its own affairs.
India follows 'Democratic Socialism', which involves a mixed economy where both public and private sectors coexist, aiming to end poverty, ignorance, and inequality of opportunity.
The State has no official religion. All religions in the country have the same status and receive equal support from the State.
Supreme power lies with the people (Democracy), and the head of the state (President) is elected directly or indirectly for a fixed tenure, not a hereditary monarch (Republic).

polity_articles.details: This is the only time the Preamble has been amended. It added three new words: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity'.

sections.title: Landmark Supreme Court Judgments on Preamble
sections.description: Crucial judicial interpretations regarding whether the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and its amendability.

historical_events.significance: The Supreme Court specifically opined that the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution.
The Supreme Court rejected its earlier ruling and held that the Preamble IS an integral part of the Constitution. It can be amended, provided the 'Basic Structure' is not altered.
The Supreme Court once again reiterated and reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.

sections.title: Salient Features of the Constitution - Part 1
sections.description: The structural, foundational, and functional characteristics that make the Indian Constitution unique.

key_concepts.explanation: Originally (1949), it contained a Preamble, 395 Articles in 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. Its vastness is due to the country's geographical diversity, historical influences (like the GoI Act 1935), and single constitution for both Centre and States.
Under Article 368, some provisions require a special majority to be amended (rigid), while others can be amended by a simple legislative majority (flexible).
It establishes a federal structure (two governments, division of powers) but contains many unitary features (strong Centre, single citizenship, all-India services).

key_associations.extra_info: Described as the Magna Carta of India, ensuring civil liberties against state encroachment (Part III).
Contained in Part IV, these are non-justiciable guidelines meant to establish a social and economic democracy (Welfare State).
Based on the principle of cooperation and coordination between the legislative and executive organs.

sections.title: Salient Features of the Constitution - Part 2
sections.description: Additional unique mechanisms, including judicial structure, voting rights, and emergency handling.

key_concepts.explanation: A single system of courts enforces both central and state laws, with the Supreme Court at the top. It is kept independent from the executive to protect citizens' rights.
Every Indian citizen above the age of 18 has the right to vote without any discrimination based on caste, race, religion, sex, or literacy.
Enables the President to meet any extraordinary situation effectively, converting the federal structure into a unitary one without formal constitutional amendment.

polity_articles.details: Reduced the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years, effective from 1989.

important_facts.fact: K.C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as 'Quasi-Federal', highlighting its unique federal-unitary blend.
